title: Wrapping SIMT increment and decrement over a fixed cycle
surface: simt_atomic_inc(cell, limit) and simt_atomic_dec(cell, limit) with their wraparound; simt_threadfence(); two @simt(num_threads=256) launches in one vec kernel, one seeding and one contributing
study_for: `LIMIT` is the top of the cycle, not its length. `simt_atomic_inc(cell, 5)` counts 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0 -- six values -- and the decrement wraps from 0 back to 5. So four contributors take the increment row from 0 to 4 and the decrement row from 5 to 1, and the reference states both as modular arithmetic over `LIMIT + 1`.

The reference counts contributors and models no thread order, which is the only honest reference for an atomic. It works here because both operations commute over the cycle: any interleaving of four increments from zero lands on four. An atomic whose result depended on the order would need either a lock or a different check.

The thread geometry is the whole input. 256 threads over 64 columns is four contributors each, and the `different_dummy` case exists to say so out loud: the dummy tensor is copied to UB to satisfy the input-tensor requirement and never read, so two different dummies must give identical output. That also means this example cannot catch a data-path defect -- it is not measuring one.

`simt_threadfence()` between the two atomics is a thread fence and is described as nothing more. It orders one thread's memory operations; it does not rendezvous threads and it is not a global barrier. The seeding is a separate launch precisely because a fence would not have been enough.
do_not_copy_when: You read `LIMIT` as a count. It is the inclusive top of the cycle, so the period is `LIMIT + 1`. Off by one here is off by one in every column.
You expect `simt_threadfence()` to synchronise threads. It does not. Ordering between threads needs the atomics themselves, a separate launch, or an all-vector rendezvous.

You want a counter whose final value tells you the contributor count. Over a cycle it tells you the count modulo `LIMIT + 1`. With more contributors than the cycle admits, several different counts give the same answer -- which is a property of a ring counter, not a defect, and is why this example's contributor count is smaller than its cycle.
